sources.title: Sakana Namazu API release
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27. The August 3, 2026 API announcement explicitly identifies Kimi K2.6 as the base and describes Japanese/business adaptation using in-house data and tuning for neutral responses. Image recognition is demonstrated. It describes no pruning, distillation, expert expansion or replacement vision encoder.

sources.title: Sakana Namazu product and FAQ
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27. FAQ 06 explicitly says Sakana starts from open Kimi K2.6 and applies additional training for Japanese performance and neutral responses. It does not describe structural changes or publish an independent Namazu parameter count.

sources.title: Exact Namazu model and API documentation
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27. Official docs bind sakana-namazu to sakana-namazu-v1.0, explicitly identify a single in-house model based on Kimi K2.6, and retain image input. They distinguish Namazu from the Fugu multi-model orchestrator; tools and file handling are service facilities. No additional neural structure or parameter count is disclosed.

sources.title: Pinned Kimi K2.6 base-model card
sources.evidence: Freshly read pinned original card, independently reopened October 27. Its Model Summary explicitly publishes 1T total and 32B activated parameters for the named Kimi K2.6 base. MoonViT is separately listed as 400M; retain the published rounded total and activated convention without inventing an additive component total. These support a labeled nominal inference for Sakana’s post-trained derivative, not a Namazu tensor census.

sources.title: Pinned Kimi K2.6 configuration
sources.evidence: Fresh pinned original fetched HTTP 200 and read October 27; identical to the same-day cache. KimiK25ForConditionalGeneration has a kimi_k2 text configuration with 61 layers, 384 routed experts, eight selected experts and one shared expert, plus the vision configuration. Corroborates the named multimodal MoE base; it is not a Namazu checkpoint configuration.

sources.title: Namazu alpha prototypes and Sakana Chat launch
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27. March 24, 2026 launches Namazu-DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus, Llama-3.1-Namazu-405B and Namazu-gpt-oss-120B prototypes through post-training. These distinct bases do not size the later explicitly Kimi K2.6-based API model.

sources.title: Sakana Chat adds Fugu and a new Namazu generation
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27. August 13, 2026 updates Chat to the new Namazu generation and links its already-available API/product. Image/document attachments and Python execution are application capabilities; no model parameter count or structural change is supplied.

sources.title: Sakana Translate adopts new-generation Namazu
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27. August 21, 2026 explicitly links the new Translate model to the generation recently released through API and Chat. It describes a refreshed base relative to the earlier generation and improved post-training; its original translation comparison evaluates quality, not total or activated parameters.

sources.title: Namazu adoption in Evidence Finder
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27. October 9, 2026 describes current Namazu as post-training that preserves base reasoning, knowledge and coding while adapting Japanese behavior. The medical evaluation and comparison statements supply no separate parameter count or evidence of pruning, distillation, expert expansion or new neural modalities.

sources.title: Sakana API platform terms
sources.evidence: Service/configuration rights remain with Sakana and relevant licensors, with permission limited to service use. This supports Proprietary hosted-model classification; the base model’s license does not grant access to Namazu weights.

sources.title: Exact Sakana-hosted Namazu endpoint metadata
sources.evidence: The Sakana AI endpoint advertises context_length262144 and max_completion_tokens65536. Text/image/file input and text output are listed. Its August11 provider identifier/listing is not the August3 original API release.

sources.title: Official SakanaAI model inventory
sources.evidence: All49 returned official models were inspected; none is a Namazu checkpoint. The67-repository public GitHub organization inventory also contains no Namazu-named repository. No exact public weights or neural configuration were located.

sources.title: Sakana research and product archive
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened archive October 27 and searched Namazu total/active parameters and structural changes in English and Japanese, including arXiv and later first-party comparison leads. No independent current-Namazu parameter table was located. Later October MASS research is a Qwen3.6-27B experiment, not a Namazu architecture disclosure; March prototype sizes and secondary catalog numbers do not establish this API model’s counts.

sources.title: Sakana AI Engineer Open House 2026
sources.evidence: Freshly read October 27. The October 21 report distinguishes its from-scratch pretraining work, Namazu post-training to adapt overseas models, and Fugu orchestration. It supplies no new Namazu size or structural-change disclosure.

sources.title: Sakana Chat Update: Fugu Max for Everyone, Now with Memory
sources.evidence: Freshly read October 27. The September 17 model replacement is explicitly Fugu Max. Namazu receives the application memory feature; this is not evidence of a replacement Namazu base or added neural parameters.

sources.title: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision
sources.evidence: Freshly checked October 27 as a later original research/comparison lead. The study and its experimental comparisons use Qwen3.6-27B and variants; no Namazu occurrence or Namazu total/activated parameter table was found. It does not establish structural changes to the hosted Namazu model.

name.note: Exact hosted API product, currently identified as sakana-namazu-v1.0; not a combined count of the March alpha prototypes.

developer.note: Sakana performs the Japanese adaptation; Moonshot AI develops the named Kimi K2.6 base.

family.note: Normalized Namazu product lineage. The family contains different base-model generations; family membership does not imply identical architecture or size.

release_date.note: Explicit release of the updated Kimi K2.6-based API model. March24 dates other alpha prototypes; August13 and21 are subsequent Chat/Translate rollouts, not the first API release.

open_weights.note: Distributed as restricted hosted API access. The base is open-weight, but no public Namazu checkpoint was identified in official inventories.

license.note: Descriptive hosted-model classification. Do not transfer Kimi K2.6’s Modified MIT license to unpublished Namazu weights or confuse service access with weight redistribution.

parameters_b.note: Nominal lineage-based inference: Sakana explicitly post-trains Kimi K2.6, whose developer publishes 1T total parameters. The API retains image input, and the reviewed launch, current documentation and later updates disclose no pruning, distillation, expert expansion or new neural modality that would defeat nominal inheritance. This is the base developer’s rounded specification, not an independently counted Namazu checkpoint; no exact derivative tensor count is claimed.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal lineage-based inference from the explicit Kimi K2.6 post-training relationship and Moonshot’s separately published 32B activated-parameter figure. This preserves the base developer’s MoE counting convention; it is not derived by equating total and active parameters. No changed expert structure or independent Namazu active-count convention was found in the bounded fresh search. Exact per-token and modality-dependent component participation remains unspecified.

architecture.note: Lineage-based inference: Sakana explicitly starts from Kimi K2.6 and applies additional training, while the pinned base card/config verify a neural MoE Transformer. This establishes the broad MoE classification, not a claim that every dimension, parameter or vision component is unchanged. No Namazu configuration is public.

context_window.note: Advertised hosted capacity: developer documents256K and the exact Sakana AI endpoint gives262144 tokens. This is a serving limit, not an independently verified native training maximum; endpoint completion cap is65536.

modalities.note: Developer documents image inputs and text responses. PDF/Office/CSV files are API containers handled through tool facilities, not separate neural modalities. No video capability is inherited from Kimi K2.6.

reasoning.note: Extended thinking is explicitly documented and enabled by default, with enable/disable controls and reasoning output. No unsupported effort levels are inferred from generic provider metadata.

tool_call.note: The model selects caller-defined functions and built-in web_search/code_interpreter tools; documentation explicitly describes autonomous tool loops. Tool execution can generate files without making media generation a neural output modality.

description.value: Japanese-language adaptation of Kimi K2.6, trained for Japanese language and business contexts with thinking and tool use.
description.note: Describes documented lineage, specialization and capabilities without unsupported benchmark-superiority claims.

patch.description: Japanese-language adaptation of Kimi K2.6, trained for Japanese language and business contexts with thinking and tool use.
patch.notes: Kimi K2.6-based Sakana Namazu API, released August 3, 2026; current model ID sakana-namazu-v1.0. Nominal 1T total and 32B activated parameters are inferred from Sakana’s explicit additional-training lineage and Moonshot’s base specification; reviewed updates describe no structural change. These are rounded published counts, not a Namazu tensor census or exact modality-specific active count. March alpha prototypes used different bases. The 262,144-token context is the advertised hosted limit. Neural modalities are text/image input and text output; files, search and code execution are API/tool facilities.

summary: Parameter re-audit: accept nominal 1000B total and 32B activated parameters as labeled inferences from Sakana’s explicit Kimi K2.6 post-training lineage and the pinned Moonshot card. Fresh original launch, FAQ, API docs, base configuration and August–October updates retain vision and disclose no pruning, distillation, expert expansion or new neural modality. Bounded total/active searches and later original research comparisons found no separate Namazu count or conflicting architecture; exact checkpoint totals and modality-dependent active participation remain unspecified. The other 12 field assessments are unchanged.
